content.label: Examiner note - why addition polymers will not rot
content.body: Addition polymers are not biodegradable because their C-C backbone is inert: microorganisms have no chemistry that attacks it, so landfill polymers persist for decades. (Condensation polyesters differ - some biopolyesters ARE biodegradable, the exception the specification names.) Disposal answers earn marks by trade-offs: burning gives energy but can release toxic gases; recycling saves feedstock but needs sorting.
